newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: Cricket - Wellington, Otago show interest in Parore.
newsitem.headline: Cricket - Wellington, Otago show interest in Parore.

text.p: AUCKLAND, Feb 11 - Both Otago and Wellington are interested in recruiting discarded New Zealand batsman Adam Parore, but they face a wall of paperwork before the unwanted Auckland cricketer can resume his first-class career, NZPA reports.
Parore's career is currently in limbo, after being sacked by Auckland for disciplinary reasons and then dropped by New Zealand due to poor form.

Otago chief executive Warren Lees, who worked with Parore during his tenure as New Zealand coach, said he would be discussing the prospect of recruiting the No 3 batsman with his chairman Bob Macdonald in Alexandra today.

"We're losing Matthew Maynard (an English professional) in about a week and we've lost some of our investment on getting Matt Horne down here from Auckland with him being picked for New Zealand," Lees said.
"That effectively curtails our batting depth and I'll be talking to the chairman to see how he, the team and its management feel about maybe getting Adam to come and play for us.
"The environment here might be more suitable if all he is looking for is to get away from it all and concentrate on his cricket."
Wellington chief executive Rodney Moore this morning confirmed that he has had informal discussions with Parore but, like Lees, he too has to moot the idea with others in the association.
"We've spoken to him, obviously he wants to play cricket because that is what he does, but there is a whole process to go through first," Moore said.
Moore added: "If we are to view Parore as a prospect we would need to work out what our requirements are and, fundamentally, do we want him as a player?
"We also have to look at our team synergy and how he would get on in our team."
Both Moore and Lees said it was now up to New Zealand Cricket (NZC), Auckland and whichever association that wanted Parore, to all agree over his transfer.
"The current rules don't allow for players to move in a season, but there is provision for NZC board to grant dispensation to a player," Moore said.
"Adam would need to apply for dispensation and he would need to satisfy NZC that he has an association to go to and that generally being granted dispensation is acceptable all round."
Auckland chief executive Lindsay Crocker said his personal view was that there was no reason why Parore should not be given a release.
"We haven't considered it yet because we haven't been asked," Crocker said.
"Obviously we'd have to discuss it collectively, but personally we wouldn't want to stand in his way."
Chairman of NZC selectors Ross Dykes said he had asked NZC to consider granting Parore dispensation.
"There has been discussion, and certainly I have been pushing his case as a matter of some urgency," Dykes said.
New Zealand's selectors, despite dropping Parore from the third test team, are keen to see him continue playing first-class cricket in case he is needed in the future.
NZC chief executive Christopher Doig said this morning that as far as the national body was concerned, Parore was still regarded as an Auckland player.
"What we've got to get from Adam and his lawyer David Howman is his application for dispensation and his argument as to why he wants to shift to another province," Doig said.
"So it is really left to him to seek dispensation in order to have him released from Auckland if he wants."
